headline: Amazon and Google will hold about 15% and just under 14% of Anthropic in IPO
body: Amazon's conversion would give it about 15% ownership of Anthropic, and Google will own just under 14%, both in non-voting shares. If Amazon converted all of its notes now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic.
note: For investors, the non-voting structure means the two cloud companies would hold large Anthropic stakes without voting power in the lab.

evidence.text: Amazon has opted to convert a chunk of them as part of the IPO into a special class of non-voting shares that will give it about 15% ownership.
Google, meanwhile, will own just under 14% (13.7%), also in non-voting shares, which come from the conversion of notes, as well as the “private placement” sale of shares as part of this IPO.
If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise).
